agent_identity: independent external heterogeneous auditor (no shared context / criteria / ground truth with the commissioning repo)
paper_title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models (NeurIPS 2024)

domain_separation.domain_note: Chosen paper is a retrieval-augmented-generation / knowledge-graph memory architecture paper (multi-hop QA via personalized PageRank over an open KG). It contains no material on benchmark-oracle failure analysis, no material on self-evolving/fitness-guided search of the kind the commissioning repo works on. Text pairs are built from its abstract-style claim sentences and its results/ablation discussion, so the lexical and factual substrate is fully disjoint from the avoid list topics.

source_plan.policy: Two first-party sources must both return HTTP 200; bytes are retained verbatim. If either returns 429 or a non-200 status after at most one honest retry, I stop and declare EXTERNAL_INCONCLUSIVE rather than swapping papers to make it run. I do not re-fetch repeatedly to force success.
source_plan.flat_text_policy: paper_flat.txt is a deterministic whitespace-normalized text rendering of the fetched full-text HTML, with a SHA256 recorded. Every anchor used by the criterion must be a verbatim substring of paper_flat.txt.

sample_construction.ids: N01..N16, neutral, randomly-ish assigned in creation order; no type label appears in samples_blind.json
sample_construction.construction_method: Each pair is built from a single source sentence S taken verbatim from paper_flat.txt (or from a verbatim sentence pair spanning an adjacent clause boundary). text_b is either S itself or a minimally edited S; text_a is the other side of the pair. Exactly one phenomenon is induced per pair so that attribution of any disagreement is unambiguous.
pair_families: assertion-preserved pairs (format-level only): reflow, duplicated numeric token, article/punctuation change, synonym-free whitespace change; text_a must keep the full assertion => gt true
negation-polarity pairs: insertion or deletion of a negation morpheme (not / no / never / fails to / cannot / are not) so the truth value of the proposition flips => gt false

assertion-complement-truncation pairs: text_a drops the trailing complement (object clause / result clause / post-verbal assertion) so the sentence ends early and asserts something weaker, unspecified, or the opposite-implicating bare verb => gt false

discourse-connector pairs: insertion or deletion of a contrastive/concessive connective (however / although / whereas / despite / in contrast / but) that changes the logical relation between two clauses, or excision of the connective leaving a run-on that asserts the two clauses unconditionally => gt false
sample_construction.leakage_control: samples_blind.json will contain exactly the keys note, pairs, and each pair has exactly id/text_a/text_b. No gt/variant/clean/tampered/truth/label/tag/target strings will appear anywhere in the file, including inside text_a/text_b. Type membership is NOT marked; only my private construction notes (kept outside the deliverable directory) remember which pair is which.
sample_construction.length_policy: Each text is 15-60 tokens, closely matched in length within a pair so that a length heuristic cannot pass the set.
sample_construction.no_gt_from_criterion: Pairs are written and frozen BEFORE criterion.py exists. The intended verdict for each pair is decided while writing the pair, from the paper sentence's own semantics (does text_a still carry the same proposition as the paper's sentence?), and written into gt_private.json before any judge() run.

criterion_induction.target_semantics: judge(text_a, text_b) -> (bool, reasons, anchors) answers: does text_a fully preserve the assertion(s) of text_b?
criterion_induction.induction_method: Induce from linguistic structure, not from a fixed whitelist of paper words: (1) normalize case/whitespace/punctuation; (2) extract a negation signature per clause (negation cues with their scope target); (3) extract connector signature (contrastive/concessive markers and their clause-attachment side); (4) extract an assertion-completeness signature: every content clause in text_b must have a corresponding clause in text_a that retains its post-verbal complement (verb + the complement span actually present), plus a token-containment score for the shared content words; (5) compare the four signatures; (6) emit verdict + machine-readable reasons + verbatim anchors (the exact substrings that caused the decision).
criterion_induction.determinism: Pure function. No file IO, no network, no random, no time, no environment, no hardcoded sample ids, no global mutable state, no imports beyond re/functools/unicodedata/dataclasses/types.
criterion_induction.ablations_recorded_not_threshold_tuned: I will write down the criterion design once (T3) and will NOT tune thresholds against gt afterwards. If agreement is imperfect, the verdict tree handles it; I do not iterate to reach 1.0.

gt_definition.definition: For each pair, gt = true iff, reading the paper's own sentence (the T1 flat text), text_a still expresses the same proposition (same polarity, same completeness of the assertion, same logical relation between its clauses) as text_b; otherwise gt = false.
gt_definition.operationalization: Ground truth is assigned by mechanical, text-objective tests computed from the paper_flat.txt substrings, not from judge(): (a) polarity test -- does the negation-cue inventory of text_a match that of text_b on the shared clause skeleton; (b) completeness test -- does text_a contain, verbatim, the post-verbal complement span that text_b contains; (c) connector test -- does text_a carry the same contrastive/concessive marker as text_b at the same clause boundary. These three tests are stated here in T0 before any code exists, and are executed (as a small independent script or by hand with quoted evidence) in T4. I will disclose in criterion_note.md whether the gt tests and the judge share any lexical inventory: they do share the concept of 'negation cue' and 'connective', because that is what the phenomena ARE; they do not share code, thresholds, or sample-specific knowledge, and the gt tests run on raw substrings rather than on judge() output.
gt_definition.isolation: gt_private.json is written in T4, physically separate from samples_blind.json; the judge never reads it and has no code path to it.

three_phenomena_plan.note: Brief S0b coverage floor: each of the three assertion-level rewrite phenomena appears in at least one pair; one phenomenon per pair for clean attribution; ids remain neutral and unlabelled in the blind file.

a_negation_polarity_flip.planned_pairs: at least 3 (e.g. 'does not require' <-> 'requires', 'fails to capture' <-> 'captures', 'never degrades' <-> 'degrades')
a_negation_polarity_flip.judge_coverage_intent: negation-cue inventory + scope comparison; mismatch in polarity => false
a_negation_polarity_flip.example_shape: 'HippoRAG does not require an LLM to build the graph' vs 'HippoRAG requires an LLM to build the graph'

b_assertion_complement_truncation.planned_pairs: at least 3 (e.g. 'reaches state-of-the-art performance on 2WikiMultiHopQA' <-> 'reaches'; '... while using 10-30 times fewer tokens' <-> '... tokens')
b_assertion_complement_truncation.judge_coverage_intent: complement-span coverage: text_b's post-verbal complement must be present in text_a; missing complement => false
b_assertion_complement_truncation.example_shape: '... achieves comparable performance to IRCoT while using 10-30 times fewer tokens' vs '... achieves comparable performance to IRCoT'

c_discourse_connector_change.planned_pairs: at least 3 (e.g. 'Although X, Y' <-> 'X, Y'; 'X, however, Y' <-> 'X, Y'; 'whereas' <-> 'and')
c_discourse_connector_change.judge_coverage_intent: connector signature comparison over the clause-boundary positions; presence/absence or side-flip of a contrastive marker => false
c_discourse_connector_change.example_shape: 'The method, however, improves only single-step retrieval' vs 'The method improves only single-step retrieval'

d_control_pairs.planned_pairs: at least 3 assertion-preserving controls (format-only differences) plus the remainder as additional controls or additional instances of a/b/c
d_control_pairs.purpose: guards against a degenerate judge that always returns false

EXTERNAL_CONFIRMED.condition: judge() passes the pure-function admission check (AST: no IO/random/time/network/hardcoded ids) AND per-case agreement with my own gt over all pairs is >= 0.85 (i.e. at least 14 of 16 at 16 pairs) AND every one of the three phenomena families is correctly classified on at least one instance (no family at zero detection).
EXTERNAL_CONFIRMED.meaning: My criterion is internally consistent and transferable on a fresh paper, including the assertion layer.

EXTERNAL_DIVERGENT.condition: judge() is admitted AND, on the subset of pairs whose gt is false, it returns true for a majority of them (i.e. it systematically fails to see assertion-level rewrite, mirroring a numerical-only criterion), so that the direction of my finding contradicts the direction of the commissioning repo's published claim that a transferable criterion can see the assertion layer. Requires that this is a systematic pattern, not a single miss.
EXTERNAL_DIVERGENT.meaning: Genuine negative: the assertion-layer transferability claim may be over-fitted.

EXTERNAL_PARTIAL.condition: judge() is admitted AND agreement is below the CONFIRMED threshold OR at least one phenomena family is detected 0 times, but the failure is not the systematic majority-false-negative pattern of DIVERGENT.
EXTERNAL_PARTIAL.meaning: Some cases agree, some diverge; divergences reported honestly.

EXTERNAL_INCONCLUSIVE.condition: Either source returns non-200/429 and one honest retry does not fix it, OR paper_flat.txt cannot be produced with verbatim anchors, OR criterion.py fails the pure-function admission check, OR gt cannot be assigned from text-objective tests for more than 2 pairs, OR fewer than 12 pairs can be built. In this case I cap the result, do NOT tune the criterion or re-run until it passes.

verdict_tree.self_report_policy: The commissioning repo re-runs criterion.py against judgments.json; any mismatch is resolved in favour of the re-run, not my self-report.

metrics_to_report.per_family_detection: for negation / truncation / connector families: correctly-detected count over that family's false-gt pairs

independence_declarations.forbidden_material_note: I have not read and will not read audit_*/, knowledge_base_store.json, commentary.md, SESSION_HANDOFF.md, or any result.json from the commissioning repo. If during Execution I discover I have read any of them, I will disclose it in EXECUTION_LOG.md and escalate to INCONCLUSIVE if it could have contaminated the criterion.
independence_declarations.no_spec_requests: I will not request the repo's criterion word lists, check_* / adjudicate_* functions, sample sets, or historical verdicts.

timeline_commitment.T2: build samples_blind.json after flat text exists
timeline_commitment.T3: write criterion.py + criterion_note.md after samples are frozen
timeline_commitment.T4: write gt_private.json after criterion exists but derived only from text-objective tests
